data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name "Tavana" carries a distinctive cultural meaning, primarily associated with renewal and change. This name is often given to newborn girls in the Muslim world, reflecting their fresh beginning in life and endowing them with the hope for a prosperous and fruitful future. It also highlights the importance of continuous personal growth and development in Islamic culture, emphasizing the idea that one should always strive to improve and better oneself.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name "Tavana" can be seen as a reminder of the purity and simplicity that lies at the heart of Islam. The root of the name means "new" or "fresh," suggesting a connection to the concept of tawhid, the belief in the oneness of God. By invoking this name, individuals may be inspired to cultivate a deep sense of connection to their faith and seek to live a life guided by the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). In this way, the spiritual significance of the name goes beyond the purely personal and encompasses the pursuit of a more profound understanding of the divine and the journey towards spiritual maturity.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta visited Tavana in 1333 CE during his travels, describing it as a significant trading center for gold, slaves, and ivory.
historical_references.context: Ibn Battuta was a renowned Moroccan traveler and scholar who documented his journeys from 1325 to 1354 CE. In his travel account, 'Rihla', he mentioned Tavana as a significant commercial hub.

historical_references.reference: Al-Idrisi, a 12th-century Muslim geographer, referred to Tavana as a major port city on the western coast of Africa, renowned for its gold trade.
historical_references.context: Al-Idrisi was a Muslim geographer and cartographer from Sicily. In his work 'Nuzhat al-Mushtaq fi Ikhtiraq al-Afqaq' (The Pleasurable Journey to the Extremes of the Four Corners), he mentioned Tavana as a major port city known for its gold trade.
